key_reasoning.reason: Base XL: 18 source modules across several subsystems. Provisioning (budgets router, provisioning_access, provisioning models, new ProvisioningBudgetService, ProvisioningService), shared budget (ProjectBudgetService check_group_request/_check_group_plan, changed-or-failed category sync, budget_enums SYNCED_STATUSES, project_budget_repository for_update lock), project/cost-center/ServiceNow services, application_repository, and the LiteLLM budget_provider_adapter. A new check-phase plus two-commit abstraction was added. Raised to XXL by the shared-core-utilities red flag.

Base L: no precedent for an all-or-nothing call that runs a read-only check phase and then two separate commits (project, then budget plus provider sync). The 500/502 resend contract relies on find-or-create idempotency, an IntegrityError retry and a group row lock against concurrent writers. Raised to XL by the authorization red flag: manage-projects is required only on some paths and is checked again inside commit 1.
Diffstat reports 35 files (4793+/1941-), which falls in the 16+ band: 18 source, 15 test (including the regenerated OpenAPI baseline) and 3 docs (AGENTS.md and two API guides).

4 layers: API (router, security dependency, request/response models), Service, DB-Persistence (row lock and entity-count queries, no schema migration) and External (LiteLLM adapter update when there is no provider ref). LiteLLM is an existing integration, so the new-external-service bump does not apply.

The nearest L example (epmcdme-10401, 22) agrees on the band. The adjacent XL example (epmcdme-10303, 27) scores Component Scope 5 for a new external integration; this change scores 6 here only because of the shared-utility red flag. Without that flag the total is 24, still L. The actual total of 25 is above the initial L 21, mainly because the file count (35 against the planned range) and the budget-service changes needed for the all-or-nothing and resend guarantees were not in the initial scope.
